meta.title: LlamaIndex for RAG
meta.thesis: LlamaIndex for RAG is practical when learners can apply it to this concrete case: A team builds a LlamaIndex RAG assistant for onboarding docs and needs traceable sources. By the end, they should be able to build or review LlamaIndex RAG pipeline with loaders, nodes, retriever, and response synthesis, measure answers include correct source nodes, and catch the failure where documents load correctly but metadata is stripped before retrieval.

mentalMap.title: LlamaIndex for RAG: mental map
mentalMap.caption: Build RAG around LlamaIndex data objects: readers, nodes, indexes, retrievers, query engines, and evaluators.
mentalMap.oneLineThesis: LlamaIndex is most valuable when the hard part is preparing, indexing, and querying private data rather than merely calling an LLM.

blocks.title: LlamaIndex is data-centric RAG plumbing

spans.text: Problem anchor: a lesson assistant must answer from curated KB notes with citations. The risky part is not the final sentence style; it is loading notes, preserving headings, creating nodes, retrieving the right context, and proving citations support claims.
LlamaIndex gives names to those steps: readers load data, parsers create nodes, indexes organize nodes, retrievers select nodes, and query engines synthesize answers.
If you cannot point to the node that supports a sentence, the RAG app is not debuggable.

blocks.analogy: LlamaIndex is a workshop for shaping source material before the model writes.

blocks.title: Worked map: five course notes to a query engine

spans.text: The app reads five Markdown notes, stores category and source URL as metadata, parses heading-based nodes, builds a vector index, and exposes a query engine with similarity_top_k=6.
A learner question about reranking retrieves nodes with heading breadcrumbs. The answer includes source titles rather than anonymous passages.

blocks.title: Parsing decides what the index can know

spans.text: A PDF with headers, a Markdown note, and a table export need different parsing care. If boilerplate, nav text, or fragmented tables become nodes, retrieval quality suffers no matter which model generates the final answer.
The loader should preserve source URL, document title, heading path, date, and permissions. The parser should keep definitions with caveats and code with prerequisites.
Print ten sample nodes and ask whether each could support a cited answer.

blocks.analogy: The index is downstream of the parser; it cannot recover missing source structure.

blocks.title: Case study: citation drift from weak nodes

spans.text: A query engine cites a note titled “Limitations,” but the displayed source title gives no topic. The fix is not a better answer prompt; it is heading metadata and node text that includes the parent title.
After metadata and parser changes, the same retrieval result becomes “RAG Evaluation > Limitations,” and reviewers can verify the claim.

blocks.title: Retrieval is not a black box

spans.text: A LlamaIndex query engine can hide several choices: which retriever, how many nodes, which metadata filters, and which postprocessors or rerankers. Each choice changes what the model sees.
For exact product versions or categories, metadata filters should narrow eligible nodes. For noisy top-k, reranking or node postprocessing can improve packed evidence.
Log retrieved node IDs, scores, metadata, and final prompt context for every evaluation query.

blocks.analogy: A query engine is a context assembly line, not a magic answer slot.

spans.text: A RAG demo that only prints the final answer is incomplete. The development slice should print retrieved node text, scores, and metadata so you can debug failures.
Spaced recall: from structured outputs, the model is not the validator. Your app should verify source support and output shape outside the model call.
Add one question whose correct response is “not enough evidence.”

blocks.title: Minimal LlamaIndex RAG skeleton
blocks.code:
from llama_index.core import Document, VectorStoreIndex

notes = [
    Document(text="Reranking reorders retrieved candidates before answer synthesis.", metadata={"source": "retrieval-eval.md"}),
    Document(text="Chunking preserves answer evidence with headings and metadata.", metadata={"source": "chunking.md"}),
]

index = VectorStoreIndex.from_documents(notes)
query_engine = index.as_query_engine(similarity_top_k=2)
response = query_engine.query("What does reranking do in a RAG system?")

print(response)
for node in response.source_nodes:
    print(node.metadata, node.score, node.text[:80])
blocks.explanation: The code builds an index, queries it, and prints source nodes so the developer can verify grounding.

blocks.title: Do not hide weak retrieval inside an agent

spans.text: If a query engine cannot reliably retrieve the right nodes for direct questions, wrapping it as an agent tool will not fix the evidence problem. It will make traces longer.

Evaluation should include direct lookup, paraphrase, exact identifiers, negative cases, and stale-source cases. The target is not just a plausible answer; it is answer text supported by retrieved nodes.
Promote recurring failed questions into the eval set before tuning the next setting.

blocks.title: Verify AI output from LlamaIndex RAG

spans.text: Use this review when reading generated answers.

items.text: The retrieved nodes contain the facts used in the answer.
Node metadata gives usable citations and source titles.
The query engine refuses or qualifies answers when evidence is absent.
Parser and chunk settings are recorded with the eval results.
Any reranker or postprocessor improves packed top-k on known failures.

blocks.prompt: When should you expose the query engine as an agent tool?

options.text: Before loading documents.

blocks.explanation: Agent loops should build on trustworthy retrieval, not conceal missing evidence.

rag.label: RAG
rag.laymanDefinition: Retrieving relevant evidence before generation so answers can be grounded in sources.
rag.technicalNote: RAG quality depends on corpus freshness, chunking, embeddings, filters, ranking, citation handling, and faithfulness evaluation.

embedding.label: Embedding
embedding.laymanDefinition: A numeric vector representation of text used for semantic comparison.
embedding.technicalNote: Embedding choices fix dimension, distance metric, query/passage formatting, model version, and migration requirements for retrieval.

vector_search.label: Vector search
vector_search.laymanDefinition: Finding nearby vectors to retrieve semantically related chunks.
vector_search.technicalNote: Vector search needs metadata filters, recall tests, index tuning, and fallback for exact terms, IDs, and rare phrases.

chunk.label: Chunk
chunk.laymanDefinition: A source text segment stored and retrieved as a unit.
chunk.technicalNote: Chunk design balances semantic completeness, citation accuracy, token budget, overlap, metadata, and update/delete behavior.

reranker.label: Reranker
reranker.laymanDefinition: A second-stage model or method that reorders retrieved candidates by relevance.
reranker.technicalNote: Rerankers improve top-result precision when candidate recall is adequate, but add latency, cost, and evaluation complexity.

rrf.label: RRF
rrf.laymanDefinition: A rank-fusion method that merges multiple result lists by reciprocal rank.
rrf.technicalNote: RRF is useful for hybrid retrieval because it combines lexical and vector rankings without requiring comparable raw scores.

finalCheck.title: Knowledge check
finalCheck.intro: A quick check across the whole lesson — pick or type your answers.

questions.prompt: In LlamaIndex's data hierarchy, which object is the smallest unit that actually gets embedded and stored in a vector index?

options.text: Document
Node
Query engine
Retriever

questions.explanation: A Document is the raw loaded file; LlamaIndex splits it into Nodes, and it is the Node that gets an embedding and lives in the index.

questions.prompt: You are loading a set of legal contracts. Each contract has a different effective date and jurisdiction. Where is the RIGHT place to store those attributes so a retriever can filter on them later?

options.text: In the query string the user sends at runtime
As node metadata attached during loading
In the LLM system prompt
In a separate SQL table outside LlamaIndex

questions.explanation: Metadata attached to nodes during loading travels with every chunk, so a metadata filter on the retriever can use it to restrict results by date or jurisdiction without touching the query text.

questions.prompt: Your RAG pipeline returns the right documents but the LLM's answer ranks a weakly relevant chunk first, burying the best evidence. Which postprocessing step is the most targeted fix?

options.text: Increase similarity_top_k to retrieve more candidates
Add a reranker postprocessor to reorder the retrieved nodes
Switch from a vector index to a keyword index
Reduce chunk size in the node parser

questions.explanation: A reranker postprocessor re-scores already-retrieved candidates and reorders them, which is exactly the right tool when the right nodes are present but misordered.

questions.prompt: After calling `query_engine.query("What is the refund policy?")`, what should you inspect BEFORE trusting the answer the LLM returns — and why?
questions.acceptableAnswer: You should inspect the source nodes (response.source_nodes) returned with the answer to verify that the evidence the LLM used actually comes from relevant chunks in your data, not from hallucination or an unrelated node.
questions.explanation: Checking source nodes lets you confirm the answer is grounded in your documents rather than fabricated by the LLM.

questions.prompt: You want to know whether your retriever is actually surfacing the chunk that contains the ground-truth answer. Which evaluation approach directly measures this?

options.text: Answer faithfulness — checking if the LLM's answer contradicts the retrieved nodes
Hit-rate / recall — checking whether the expected node appears in the retrieved context
Chunk size ablation — comparing answers with different node sizes
Latency benchmarking — measuring how fast the query engine responds

questions.explanation: Hit-rate (retrieval recall) directly measures whether the node that contains the correct answer is present in the packed context, which is the retrieval-level check before you even involve the LLM.
